source_findings.finding: EXCHPOL positive index selects atom class, not atom type. kexpol assigns kpep/prepep/dmppep/lpep; kpolar counts nonzero springs independently of lpep and enables use_expol. Water O positive spring enables the solver even when all sites are passive.

polscale starts identity; pair eligibility is lpep(i) OR lpep(k); both sites receive their own spring times shared overlap and rhat outer product. Metal-active/O-passive therefore modifies O, while metal spring0 leaves the metal tensor unchanged. O-O has no eligible active site; metal-H shared size0 yields zero.

For S2U, S=(1+b*r/2+(b*r/2)^2/3)*exp(-b*r/2), and s2=size_i*size_k*S^2. Choosing k=q/S^2(2.5) gives dimensionless radial inverse-polarizability incrementq at the normalization radius, provided switching scale is1 there.

alterpol runs before mutual induction. polinv sets the initial estimate and polscale enters the mutual solver diagonal/operator. This is a geometry-dependent tensor response, not a post hoc additive energy correction; the intrinsic scalar polarity is unchanged.

Energy uses induced dipoles solved under modified tensors; epolar1 adds dexpol chain-rule terms after the standard gradient. dexpol includes radial overlap derivatives, tensor orientation/torque terms, cutoff derivative and balanced site forces/virial.

pure_water_invariance: With no active metal or other active flags, every pair is ineligible and polscale remainsI; dexpol pair contributions vanish. Global use_expol may still be true because O spring is positive, so the numerical path differs; source supports mathematical invariance, not guaranteed bitwise identity. Actual pure-water energy/force replay remains required.
interpretation: Each metal-water dimer is changed as well as the full shell. Mutual induced dipoles couple the responses across waters, so B can change without an explicit many-body count term; this does not make the intervention B-only or prove that it repairs the observed reference discrepancy.
